profile-description: Data Engineer with 5+ years building scalable cloud data platforms on AWS & GCP. Recently graduated from NYU (MS CE, 2026). Former Data Engineer II @ NBCUniversal — Olympics reporting 60 mins ahead of SLA, 30% cost cut, ~75% faster delivery.
about-tagline: Seeking to turn your toughest data problems into faster, cheaper, automated solutions.

about-me.para1: Hey — I'm Abhishek. For the last 5+ years, I've built scalable, resilient cloud data solutions on AWS & GCP — leading migrations and automating operations with Python, SQL, Spark, Airflow, Snowflake, and Databricks.
about-me.para2: I just finished my M.S. in Computer Engineering at NYU (May 2026, GPA 3.5) and served as a Research Assistant — speeding up processing ~5x on ~2 TB of MIT SuperCloud HPC telemetry and generating GPU power traces (peak Corr = 0.93) for datacenter forecasting. Based in San Jose, CA and open to full-time Data Engineer roles.
about-me.para3: At NBCUniversal, I progressed from Data Engineer I → II. As DE II, I delivered C-suite Olympics'24 ad-performance reports 60 mins ahead of SLA with zero breaches, cut monthly cost 30% by leading a team of 5 to migrate 40+ on-prem jobs to Spark on EMR Serverless, and built an Airflow framework that now powers 30+ pipelines across linear, digital, and CTV. Earlier, I cut pipeline delivery time ~75% with one-click, SQL-driven features for audience overlap and ETL over 150M+ household records.
about-me.para4: I also ship product-minded side work — from JobSimp, a Manifest V3 Chrome extension with RAG-powered job autofill, to decade-scale NYC housing sales analytics. I care about cost-aware compute, zero-breach SLAs, and pipelines that don't wake you up at 3 AM.

1.name: JobSimp
1.description: Manifest V3 Chrome extension that cut per-job application time from ~20 mins to a few minutes — one-click autofill, automated tracking, and job filtering for 30+ applications a day. Scores any posting with a fit verdict and match/miss breakdown, then tailors resume, cover letter, and essay answers via RAG over an IndexedDB property graph, keeping Gemini/Claude/OpenAI token usage low per application.

2.name: HPC Telemetry Lakehouse & Power-Forecasting Pipeline
2.description: NYU research: sped up processing ~5x on ~2 TB of MIT SuperCloud telemetry (460K+ jobs) with a medallion lakehouse on a 16-node Spark cluster — AQE, partitioning, and skew handling. A sliding-window autoregressive diffusion transformer conditioned on SLURM job metadata generates GPU power traces for 4,400+ unseen jobs (peak Corr = 0.93) for datacenter power forecasting before jobs run.

3.name: C-Suite Olympics'24 Migration
3.description: NBCUniversal DE II rotation: delivered executive ad-performance reports 60 mins ahead of SLA with zero breaches through the Paris Games. Led a team of 5 to migrate 40+ on-prem jobs to Spark (Scala) on EMR Serverless — cutting monthly cost 30% and ending daily failures. Built an Airflow orchestration framework that absorbed a 60% scope expansion and now powers 30+ pipelines across linear, digital, and CTV on an Iceberg lakehouse with Redshift.

4.name: Audience Insights Hub
4.description: NBCUniversal DE I rotation (NBCUnified · Performance Insights Hub): cut pipeline delivery time ~75% with one-click, SQL-driven features for audience overlap, segment activation, and ETL — letting business teams match 150M+ household records without a data engineer. Shared business-name catalog and zero-copy sharing connected siloed departments; SLA-based cluster presets cut compute cost up to ~20%; CCPA/PII purge jobs and RBAC governed compliance across data clean rooms.

5.name: Schema-Grounded Enterprise Retrieval (RAG)
5.description: Schema-grounded RAG assistant (React/Flask, CI/CD) unifying text-to-SQL and document Q&A by retrieving over a graph metadata catalog (KeyBERT-indexed) — grounding SQL to real tables/columns and citation-backed answers from docs, wikis, and PDFs. SQL validation before execution and event-driven metadata refresh counter knowledge drift — one RBAC-governed interface cutting analyst self-service from ~30 minutes to under a minute.

6.name: Churn Prediction & Incentive Engine
6.description: End-to-end AWS pattern for churn: curated features in S3, SageMaker training and batch scoring, DynamoDB for low-latency scores, and Lambda functions driving a real-time incentive and segmentation service for lifecycle campaigns and experiments.

7.name: NYC Housing Sales (2015–2025)
7.description: NYU coursework: turned ~900K messy NYC Dept. of Finance property-sale records into a clean, analysis-ready lakehouse — resolving inconsistent schemas, malformed addresses, and duplicate parcels. Traced a decade of price-per-sqft, sales-volume, and affordability shifts in an interactive Tableau dashboard by borough, neighborhood, and price tier.

8.name: Alt-Currency Automation
8.description: NBCUniversal DE II rotation: automated currency-partner ingestion with zero failed runs and lower compute cost — buffering late, out-of-order inbound batches into one parallelized orchestration. Standardized 15–20 partner pipelines (VideoAmp, EDO) exchanging millions of daily impression records with a team of 7. Shipped event-driven ingestion (S3 → SQS → Lambda → Airflow → EMR → Redshift) with CI/CD and zero manual deployments.
